title: Check: namespaces, contexts and quotas
description: Five questions on scoping, switching and limiting.

options.text: A scope for names, plus a handle for quotas and access control

questions.explanation: Namespaces scope names and give RBAC and ResourceQuota something to attach to. They are not a network boundary - that is what NetworkPolicy is for.

questions.prompt: Which of these are cluster-scoped rather than namespaced? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: `kubectl api-resources --namespaced=false` lists them. ConfigMaps are namespaced; nodes, PVs and namespaces themselves are not.

questions.prompt: Write the command that makes `dev` the default namespace for your current context.
questions.explanation: Setting it once beats typing `-n dev` on every command, and it is one of the highest-value habits in a timed exam.

questions.prompt: A namespace has a ResourceQuota for CPU. A Pod is created with no resource requests. What happens?

options.text: It is rejected, because the quota requires requests to be set
It gets the namespace default of one CPU
The quota is ignored for Pods

questions.explanation: Once a quota covers a resource, every Pod in that namespace must declare requests for it - otherwise the quota could not be enforced. A LimitRange can supply the defaults.

questions.prompt: What happens to the objects inside a namespace you delete?
questions.explanation: Deleting a namespace deletes everything in it. It is the fastest cleanup there is, and the easiest way to lose work you meant to keep.
